As a leading global financial services company at the heart of the global financial system, we influence nearly 20% of the world’s investible assets. Every day, our teams harness cutting-edge AI and breakthrough technologies to collaborate with clients, driving transformative solutions that redefine industries and uplift communities worldwide.Recognized as a top destination for innovators, BNY is where bold ideas meet advanced technology and exceptional talent. Skills you will buildMarketing and brand strategy fundamentalsContent development and campaign supportResearch, analysis, and audience insight generationCollaboration, communication, and creative problem-solving Impact you will have at BNYHelp support campaigns and content that strengthen BNY’s brand presence and connect with key audiences.Contribute to work that helps teams tell a clear, consistent, and compelling story across the enterprise.Support initiatives that improve client engagement, employee advocacy, and marketing effectiveness.See how strategic marketing helps drive growth and shape the experience of a global financial services brand. Why this could be a fit for youThis role is a great fit if you are creative, curious, and interested in storytelling, branding, and strategic communication. It is well suited for someone who enjoys working across teams, developing ideas, and helping bring campaigns and content to life. Summer Internship Program The BNY Summer Internship Program offers high-potential students a dynamic 10-week experience designed to accelerate development, build professional networks, and provide meaningful exposure to one of the world's leading financial services institutions. jobs.title: Brand Insights Intern at Skipper AI
jobs.description: Employer: Skipper AI Expires: 10/10/2026 Brand Insights Intern Position Title: Brand Insights InternTarget Start Date: September 28, 2026Department: MarketingHours per Week: 5-12 hrsDuration: 6 MonthsApplication Deadline: September 21, 2026Immediate Supervisor: James LuceySupervisor Title: Chief Operating OfficerCompensation: HourlyRange: $15-$20 an hour, based on experience. Position summaryThe Brand Insights Intern at Skipper AI turns real information and stories into content that builds the Skipper brand. You're a creative writer at heart, motivated to represent Skipper AI's brand voice and pursue projects across marketing and content that bring that voice to life. You'll manage your own schedule and project-manage your own work, coordinating effectively with internal stakeholders and, where relevant, external ones as well. At the center of the role is a simple skill: taking raw information and turning it into insights and stories that align with where Skipper's brand and marketing are headed. This is a role for someone who wants their creativity to shape how a real company is seen. Success factorsManages their own schedule and workload while staying in sync with internal stakeholders.Comfortable turning raw information into a clear, compelling narrative.Genuinely curious and observant, picks up on details worth turning into a story.Organized enough to track multiple ideas and projects at different stages at once.Strongly represents Skipper AI's brand voice across everything they create. Required qualifications | Position competencies & skillsComfortable with ambiguity and figuring out the best approach for an idea.Organized and disciplined enough to track multiple ideas and projects simultaneously without losing the thread.Self-directed and accountable, takes ownership of their work and pursues critiques with a positive growth mindset.Quick to pick up new tools, will be onboarded on Jira, Confluence, and the platforms Skipper AI uses.Comfortable in an early-stage environment where priorities shift and not everything is defined yet. Preferred qualificationsHas independently started and carried a creative project through to completion, a blog, content series, or channel of their own.Experience with content or design tools, comfortable figuring things out without step-by- step guidance.Interest in marketing, branding, or storytelling for a business.Interest in video, design, or other creative mediums beyond writing.Curiosity about how brands build trust and reputation over time. Position responsibilitiesContent creation Create approved content in various formats, written, visual, video, or otherwise.Maintain Skipper AI's brand voice across everything you contribute to.Pursue projects with the expectation of iterating through drafts, incorporating feedback, and refining work through to final approval.Track the impact published pieces have on the company. Idea development and pitching Turn raw information and observations into content pitches.Collaborate with Skipper AI leadership and stakeholders to prioritize relevant projects while maintaining a backlog of ideas for later.Log and track pitches through the approval process, from idea to in- progress to published. Internal communication and check-ins Join regular check-ins with internal stakeholders to stay aligned on priorities and ideas.Write up takeaways and actionable items from meetings and conversations.Communicate proactively on scheduling conflicts, blockers, or shifts in priority. What you will gainA real portfolio of published creative work.Direct access to leadership and how brand decisions actually get made.Hands-on experience turning raw ideas into finished, public-facing content.A front-row seat to how a young AI consultancy builds its brand from the ground up.Practice pitching and defending your own creative ideas in a real business setting.Trackable KPIs and outcomes from the content you contribute to. Work designationThis position is fully remote. All core responsibilities are performed independently and do not require a fixed on-site schedule.The team looks for opportunities to meet in person when project timelines and individual schedules align. These gatherings are intentional but informal, driven by shared momentum rather than a fixed cadence. Skipper AI core valuesTrust and Transparency. We communicate openly, follow through on commitments, and treat every client and colleague with honesty. Trust is the foundation of every relationship we build. Humble Hunger. There's more to a failed task than the task itself; every mistake carries a lesson, and progress in anything is still progress forward. It's okay to be wrong, as long as you admit it. What matters is being hungry more often than you are wrong. Have Hard Conversations. One's success in life is directly correlated to their ability to have hard conversations. Conversations are hard if you are passionate, and two passionate people in a room is a rare thing. About Skipper AIIn the last year, we have worked with 8 companies, on countless projects, and have shipped things that did and didn't work. Importantly, we have captured the themes behind what leads to success or failure, and have not found a use case since those learnings did not apply. Skipper AI exists to not skip them. We've driven 90%+ adoption not because of the platform we picked, but because we refuse to skip the intentional steps. Intentionality through change has never been more important. The tools are the easy part; it's the steps most firms rush past, the change management in between where AI actually sticks or quietly dies.

Expires: 10/10/2026 Project Management InternPosition SummaryThe Project Management Intern supports the safe, efficient, and profitable delivery of electrical construction projects while learning how work moves from estimate and preconstruction through field execution, billing, closeout, and customer follow-up. Working alongside Project Managers, project support team members, field leaders, Estimating, VDC, Prefabrication, Safety, and other partners, the intern assists with project documentation, planning, coordination, material and vendor follow-up, cost awareness, and communication. The internship is designed to provide meaningful project ownership at an appropriate level while building the technical, business, and professional skills needed for an early-career role within Pieper.Values and Ways of WorkingAt Pieper Electric, we believe in the Power to Serve and the Pursuit of Excellence. Interns are expected to demonstrate a Servant's Heart, Wisdom, Integrity, Courage, Humility, and Passion in how they learn, communicate, support the field, and serve customers and teammates. Essential ResponsibilitiesSafety and Field Engagement:Complete required safety orientation and follow all company, customer, and jobsite requirements.Participate in jobsite walks, pre-planning discussions, and hazard-recognition activities with supervision.Promote open communication between field and office teams regarding safety concerns, required information, and work-planning needs.Observe how safety, quality, schedule, productivity, and cost decisions affect one another during project execution. Project Documentation and Coordination:Help obtain, organize, and maintain drawings, specifications, addenda, submittals, RFIs, meeting notes, correspondence, schedules, and other project records.Assist with project startup, estimating handoff, document control, routine reporting, and coordination of defined action items.Support permits, inspections, utility-locate requests, site access needs, and other project-specific requirements as assigned.Track job activity, including materials, equipment, resources, deadlines, and open items; communicate status and potential issues promptly. Preconstruction and Technical Planning:Support basic quantity takeoffs, bid-package preparation, scope review, and comparison of plans, specifications, and addenda.Learn how Estimating, design, layout, VDC/BIM, prefabrication, Trimble/Total Station, scheduling, and operations planning support field installation.Assist with coordination of design, layout, assembly details, prefabrication documentation, and project planning tasks as appropriate to the assignment.Help prepare for project kickoff and participate in the transition of project information from estimating to operations. Planning, Scheduling, and Resource Support:Participate in weekly planning and project meetings; document decisions, owners, deadlines, and follow-up items.Update approved trackers and schedules and help identify constraints that may affect safety, productivity, quality, cost, or completion dates.Support coordination of materials, tools, equipment, information, and internal resources needed by the project team and field.Learn how Project Managers forecast work, monitor progress, and adjust plans based on project conditions. Materials, Vendors, and Project Controls:Request and organize vendor or subcontractor information and quotes as directed; support purchase-order and material-tracking processes within assigned authority.Compile information for material purchases, submittals, delivery coordination, and operation and maintenance manuals.Assist with approved cost coding, expense tracking, billing documentation, change-order logs, and other project-control activities.Develop an understanding of budget, committed cost, labor productivity, forecast, billing, collections, cash flow, and project profitability without independently approving transactions. Communication, Service, and Team Collaboration:Communicate professionally with project managers, field leaders, craftspeople, customers, vendors, and internal partners.Prepare clear meeting notes, status updates, reports, presentations, and project correspondence for review.Provide timely, accurate service and escalate questions, conflicts, customer concerns, and project risks to the appropriate leader.Seek feedback, demonstrate curiosity, protect confidential information, and contribute ideas that improve team coordination and project outcomes. Closeout and Continuous Improvement:Assist with punch-list tracking, as-built documentation, operation and maintenance manuals, warranty information, final billing support, and closeout packages.Help confirm that required project records are complete, accurate, organized, and transferred or archived appropriately.Participate in lessons-learned discussions and complete an internship capstone that recommends or demonstrates a practical project improvement. QualificationsCurrently pursuing an associate or bachelor’s degree in construction management, Construction Science, Electrical or Mechanical Engineering, Building Science, Business, or a related field; equivalent technical education or relevant experience may be considered.Interest in electrical construction, project management, estimating, engineering, or field operations.Basic proficiency with Microsoft Office, including Excel, Word, Outlook, and Teams; willingness to learn company project systems and technical tools.Ability to travel locally to project sites and work in both office and active construction environments, as the assignment requires.Core Skills and BehaviorsPositive safety attitude and personal integrity - both are non-negotiable.Curiosity, initiative, accountability, and willingness to ask questions and apply feedback.Clear verbal and written communication with strong attention to detail.Ability to organize multiple priorities, maintain accurate records, and meet deadlines.Respectful, service-oriented approach when working with field and office employees, customers, and vendors.Work Environment and Physical RequirementsThe internship includes office and jobsite work. Office responsibilities may require extended periods of sitting, standing, and computer use. Jobsite visits may involve walking or standing for extended periods, stairs or uneven surfaces, outdoor conditions, noise, and required personal protective equipment. Reasonable accommodation may be made for qualified individuals.

jobs.title: Golf Internship @ Bandon Dunes Golf Resort at Bandon Dunes Golf Resort
jobs.description: Employer: Bandon Dunes Golf Resort Expires: 10/14/2026 As a Golf Intern at Bandon Dunes Golf Resort, you'll get real hands-on experience at one of the world's top golf destinations while pursuing your Professional Golf Management degree. You'll work directly with guests, manage our golf shop, coordinate tournaments, and learn the business side of golf operations. This isn't just shadowing someone—you'll have actual responsibilities that matter to our guests' experiences on courses that rank among the top 16 public courses in America.About Bandon Dunes Golf Resort:Bandon Dunes is a world-class golf resort located on the Oregon Coast near the charming community of Bandon. Guests come to experience golf as it was meant to be at Bandon Dunes' six distinct golf courses. That includes five 18-hole courses, which all rank among the top 16 public courses in the United States, according to Golf Digest. The resort is also home to an award-winning par-3 course, Bandon Preserve. A second par-3 course, Shorty's, will open in 2024. The two short courses are 'Courses with a Mission,' with all net proceeds funding the Bandon Dunes Charitable Foundation. The Foundation supports communities along the South Coast of Oregon.Beyond premier golf, guests delight in a variety of dining options at Bandon Dunes’ collection of restaurants. Whether you're looking to enjoy locally-sourced, Pacific-Northwest cuisine accompanied by an award-winning wine list, or prefer kicking back in a Scottish-style setting with traditional pub fare and local microbrews, there is something for everyone.Working at Bandon Dunes is a dream for golf fans, outdoor enthusiasts, and hospitality professionals alike. The Bandon Dunes team works together to create trips of a lifetime for our guests. We are passionate stewards of our resort, our community, and our environment. As an endlessly curious group, we ask questions, share ideas, and always look for a better way. With a hard-working attitude, we help guide our guests through their pure golf experience, immersed in Oregon’s natural beauty and away from the demands of daily life.What You'll Do:Learn the retail side of golf. You'll become an expert on our golf shop merchandise, help guests find what they need, and handle special orders. This means understanding products well enough to make real recommendations, not just ringing up sales.Handle real transactions. You'll process merchandise sales, greens fees, and equipment rentals while keeping accurate records. You'll learn the financial side of golf operations through actual daily work, not textbook theory.Provide genuine customer service. You'll answer guest questions, schedule tee times, and maintain professional phone interactions. When guests call, you'll be the voice they hear representing Bandon Dunes.Support tournaments and events. You'll help organize competitions and special events, coordinating between different departments to make sure everything runs smoothly. This is where you'll see how all the moving pieces fit together.Manage inventory and operations. You'll help keep merchandise displays organized, assist with inventory counts, and support various services like handicapping systems and driving range operations.What Makes You a Great Fit:You're pursuing a Professional Golf Management degree. We work with certified PGM programs and prefer students who can commit to a 6-month internship. This gives you enough time to really learn the business, not just get a quick overview.You communicate well. Strong written and verbal skills matter here because you'll interact with guests from around the world. You need to sound professional on the phone and explain complex golf services clearly.You can handle multiple priorities. Golf operations move fast, and you'll need to manage several tasks while staying calm under pressure. If you get flustered easily when things get busy, this probably isn't the right fit.You're flexible with your schedule. Golf doesn't stop for weekends or holidays. You'll work evenings, weekends, and busy periods when our guests need us most.Special Intern Benefits:Shared staff housing available for a reasonable fee, mentorship from industry professionals, and the chance to play golf for free on seven award-winning courses.If you're serious about a career in golf and want to learn the business at one of the world's premier destinations, we'd like to hear from you. This internship will give you real experience you can't get in a classroom, plus the chance to build relationships with industry professionals. You'll work hard, but you'll also get to play some of the best golf of your life on your days off.Ready to embark on an enriching journey in the world of golf? Apply today to become a Golf Intern at Bandon Dunes Golf Resort and be part of a team dedicated to providing one of the world’s most exceptional golfing experiences.At Bandon Dunes Golf Resort, we are proud to be an equal-opportunity employer. We value diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

jobs.title: Getty Post-Baccalaureate Conservation Internship at J. Paul Getty Trust
jobs.description: Employer: J. Paul Getty Trust Expires: 10/15/2026 The Getty Post-Baccalaureate Conservation Internships aim to increase the number of students from underrepresented backgrounds preparing to enroll in graduate degree programs related to museum conservation. An advanced degree is essential to a conservation career and few programs exist. Applicants often boost their credentials by completing prerequisite courses and undertaking up to thousands of hours of conservation training, usually unpaid. Graduate program administrators say these realities have limited opportunities for underrepresented groups.Launched in 2020 as a pilot program, the Getty Post-Baccalaureate Internships are the first nationwide effort to provide yearlong financial support and hands-on conservation experience to underrepresented post-baccalaureates who are preparing to apply to conservation graduate programs. EligibilityWhile these internships are intended for students from backgrounds underrepresented in the conservation field, Getty encourages eligible candidates from all backgrounds to apply for consideration. Getty is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of any protected trait under the law. Candidates will have the opportunity to demonstrate their interest in museum conservation and how they might add new and underrepresented perspectives, which can include – among other things – socio-economic status, cultural background, physical or other disability, geographical origin, and/or any other life experiences.Candidates must:-Be a United States citizen or permanent resident eligible to work in the United States (permanent residents are non-citizens authorized to live and work in the United States on a permanent basis, also known as "green card" holders). Those with DACA (Deferred Action for Childhood Arrival) status valid through the internship period are also eligible.-Be committed to a career in conservation and possess a strong desire to attend graduate school to further that goal.-Be able to demonstrate previous experience in conservation. Terms of the GrantAll positions are full-time for 12 months from September 7, 2027 — August 25, 2028. Interns are placed at conservation studios and labs at the Getty Center or Getty Villa for their first six months, and then at a local Los Angeles museum or within a different Getty department for the second six months.Grant AmountThe grant amount is $45,500 for 12 months plus $1,500 towards relocation expenses to Los Angeles. The internship includes an additional $4,000 towards educational reimbursements, certificate courses in conservation, domestic conservation conference attendance, or other professional-development opportunities related to the internship. Housing is not provided. Interns are eligible to enroll in Getty's healthcare plan at a subsidized cost. Please note that grant funds may be subject to federal and state taxes and deductions.Prerequisite Course for Graduate SchoolDuring spring 2028, interns may enroll in a prerequisite course (chemistry, art history, studio art, and/or foreign language) at a local community college to help fulfill the requirements for their graduate school applications. In addition to support from their supervisors, interns will also have the support of an academic advisor Collaborating InstitutionsInternships are offered at the conservation studios and labs at the Getty Center in Los Angeles and the Getty Villa in Malibu, along with local Los Angeles museums. For the 2027-2028 internship year, placements are being offered at the following Getty departments and institutions:Getty Conservation Institute Collections Department and Los Angeles County Museum of ArtGetty Conservation Institute Science Department and The HuntingtonGetty Research Institute Conservation and Preservation Department and the Autry Museum of the American WestJ. Paul Getty Museum Antiquities Conservation Department and the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences Margaret Herrick Library

jobs.title: USGA Golf Museum Special Collections Intern at United States Golf Association
jobs.description: Employer: United States Golf Association Expires: 10/17/2026 The USGA is a mission-based golf organization whose purpose is to unify the golf community through handicapping and grassroots programs; to showcase the game’s best talent through the U.S. Open, U.S. Women’s Open and 13 other national championships and our museum; to provide unbiased global governance with The R&A through the playing, equipment and Amateur Status rules; and to advance issues important to golf’s future, with a focus on driving sustainability, accessibility and inclusion. As a nonprofit association, our work and our team are driven to act for the good of the game. The USGA’s headquarters are located in Liberty Corner, NJ, with a recently opened campus in Pinehurst, NC. For more, visit usga.org. About this role: The USGA Golf Museum and Library seeks a recent graduate or currently enrolled student in Library Science or Archival Studies for a paid internship in the nation’s oldest sports museum. Founded in 1936, the USGA Golf Museum is the world’s leading institution for the collection, preservation, interpretation and dissemination of golf history. Since 1936, the Museum has connected golfers, sports fans and scholars with remarkable artifacts, documents, images and stories that chronicle golf’s rich history. The USGA Special Collections contain over 500,000 catalogued items including championship and personal archives, institutional records, rare books, club histories, yardage guides, comic books, fiction, poetry, historic and contemporary periodicals, instruction, biographies, newspapers, sheet music, comic books, cookbooks, programs, tour guides, directories, reference material, green section material, golf course care and maintenance, historic dealer and manufacturer catalogs for clothing, gear, and equipment, and more documenting the history of the game and all of its aspects in more than 10 languages and from around the world. Original material dates from 1566 with the Scottish Acts of Parliament to the present day. Items are used for both exhibits and research to inform content and create scholarship on the history and future of the game. The USGA Golf Museum Special Collections Intern will assist with numerous projects supporting the Special Collections. S/he will gain valuable experience in several areas of library operations including hands-on work with historic materials, describing and cataloging material in a digital repository, digitization of archival material, research, and other tasks within the USGA Special Collections. This internship is a unique opportunity to gain hands-on experience archiving, preserving and making available to the public materials on the history of golf. What you’ll do:Collections Processing and CatalogingSupport all aspects of archival collections processing including arrangement, description and cataloging materials in the Museum’s collections management system, TMS CollectionsDevelop familiarity with the TMS Record Style Guide to standardize existing TMS records for Library and Special Collections recordsSupport the Library and Special Collections digitization program by digitizing archival material and ensuring proper metadata cataloging in TMS Collections and TMS Media StudioAdditional collections processing projects as directedCollections ManagementEnsure proper housing of archival materialsSupport movement and reshelving of materials across all collections storage locationsAdditional collections management projects as directedResearch and EngagementAssist with research requests and onsite research visitsSupport the preparation and organization of assets for Museum exhibitions and projects to promote the collections Additional research projects as directed Where you’ll be: This role will be based at our Liberty Corner, NJ campus, working approximately 20 hours per week, ideally with 3 days per week on-site, between Monday - Friday. An academic semester is requested though opportunity exists for a 12-month internship. What you bring:Currently enrolled or recent graduate of a graduate level program in Library ScienceBasic knowledge of digital asset management systemsBasic knowledge of metadata, library standards and resources, and a desire to assist in preservation and access of library materialAbility to lift and move library materials up to 25 poundsBasic knowledge of best practices in handling sensitive and historic materialsPassion and enthusiasm for history and the care of historic materialsAppreciation and interest in sports heritage and/or the game of golf Compensation: The rate of pay is $20 per hour, plus overtime in accordance with applicable New Jersey law. The USGA is an equal opportunity employer. Our organization believes we are stronger by embracing our diverse backgrounds and perspectives, promoting equity so all teammates can excel and grow in their careers, and fostering experiences to drive inclusion in our workplace and game. Golf is a game for everyone, and you are always welcome.

jobs.description: Employer: Dow Jones News Fund Expires: 10/17/2026 The Dow Jones News Fund (DJNF) internship program has a legacy of excellence dating back to 1960. Each year DJNF arranges paid internships for approx. 80 college students across the country and provides them with advanced hands-on training, industry mentors and a robust peer and alumni network to tap into.Interns attend one-week training programs before reporting to work in paid internships at top media companies for 10 to 12 weeks. Weekly salaries start at $525. (Median salary is $675/week)Applicants can choose which internship programs they would like to be considered for:+ Audience Engagement: These internships vary by newsroom, but the mission always remains the same—to help the news find its audience. From writing SEO-friendly headlines and producing engaging content for video and social to crafting newsletters and seizing on trending topics on social media, job expectations vary. Previous internship placements include: Palm Beach Post, The Marshall Project, Oakland Voices and Houston Chronicle.+ Business Reporting: We place reporters in more than 30 newsrooms across the country covering a wide variety of topics from Wall Street to Main Street, including markets, economic trends, new businesses, emerging entrepreneurs, labor unions, real estate, climate change, agriculture and automotive industries. Previous internship placements include: The Wall Street Journal, American City Business Journals, Barron’s, Insider, Fortune, American Banker, Detroit News and Automotive News.+ Data Journalism: There are three different types of data internships we usually place interns in: 1) heavy emphasis on filing records requests and analyzing data using spreadsheets; 2) reporting and writing using government data or assisting investigative reporting projects; and 3) using coding and technical tools to build apps and interactive visuals for news stories. Previous internship placements include: Arkansas Democrat-Gazette, Detroit News, Maryland Matters and Investigative Reporting Workshop.+ Digital Media: Working as a digital media intern means many different things, depending on the newsroom. You could be working in print, social, video, audio or all of it. Interns receive across-the-board training so they can expand their skill sets using the latest technology and storytelling techniques. Previous internship placements include: Hawaii Public Radio, Kansas City Public Television, Oakland Voices and Storyful.+ Multiplatform Editing: Editors are the final check on a story before it is published. Multiplatform editing interns assess copy for accuracy, completeness, tone and style while also writing SEO-friendly headlines and designing pages on deadline. Previous internship placements include: The New York Times, Los Angeles Times, The Washington Post, Stars & Stripes and San Francisco Chronicle.The pre-internship training dates typically fall between May 17-June 12. Internships traditionally start the first or second week of June.

jobs.title: USGA Golf Museum and World Golf Hall of Fame Collections Intern at United States Golf Association
jobs.description: Employer: United States Golf Association Expires: 10/17/2026 The USGA is a mission-based golf organization whose purpose is to unify the golf community through handicapping and grassroots programs; to showcase the game’s best talent through the U.S. Open, U.S. Women’s Open and 13 other national championships and our museum; to provide unbiased global governance with The R&A through the playing, equipment and Amateur Status rules; and to advance issues important to golf’s future, with a focus on driving sustainability, accessibility and inclusion. As a nonprofit association, our work and our team are driven to act for the good of the game. The USGA’s headquarters are located in Liberty Corner, NJ, with a recently opened campus in Pinehurst, NC. For more, visit usga.org. About this role The USGA Golf Museum and World Golf Hall of Fame seeks a recent graduate or currently enrolled student in Museum Studies for a paid internship in the nation’s oldest sports museum. Founded in 1936, the USGA Golf Museum is the world’s leading institution for the collection, preservation, interpretation and dissemination of golf history. Since 1936, the Museum has connected golfers, sports fans and scholars with remarkable artifacts, documents, images and stories that chronicle golf’s rich history. The Museum Collection comprises more than 85,000 catalogued objects documenting the history of golf from its origins to the present. Included in the collection are artifacts from some of the most important moments in the history of championship golf. Highlights of the collection include Alan Shepard’s Moon Club; works of art by Rembrandt, Norman Rockwell, Andy Warhol, Salvador Dali and Roy Lichtenstein; a trophy from the 1904 Olympic games; rare and significant artifacts from World Wars I and II and an extensive collection of memorabilia from U.S. Presidents. The Museum Collections Intern will assist with numerous projects supporting the Museum Collection. S/he will gain valuable experience in several areas of collections care including hands-on work related to object handling, cataloging and rehousing of collections. The Museum Collections Intern will assist the collections team in the large-scale rehousing and reorganization project and can expect to make significant contributions to improving data standardization and storage conditions. This internship is a unique opportunity to gain hands-on experience working with a unique museum collection. What you’ll do:Collections CareAssist with long-term, large-scale collections projects including rehousing and cataloging of artifactsSupport rehousing and movement of materials across all collections storage locationsSupport collections team in receiving and releasing shipments, packing artifacts for transport and condition reportingSupport collections team in gallery maintenance through climate monitoring and integrated pest managementAdditional collections management projects as directed Collections Processing and CatalogingCataloging materials in the Museum’s collection’s management system, TMS CollectionsDevelop familiarity with the TMS Record Style Guide to standardize existing TMS records for Museum records Additional cataloging projects as directed Where you’ll beThis role will be based at our Liberty Corner, NJ campus, working approximately 20 hours per week, ideally with 3 days per week on-site, between Monday - Friday. The intern should be able to commit to at least one full semester. What you bringCurrently enrolled student or recent graduate of an MA program in Museum Studies or related fieldAbility to work independently with strong organizational skills and attention to detailAbility to think creatively and thoughtfully when faced with unique storage needs and willingness to voice opinions on housing methodsWillingness to work collaboratively with team membersProficiency in Microsoft Office productsExperience with museum databases a plusCompensation: The rate of pay is $20 per hour, plus overtime in accordance with applicable New Jersey law. The USGA is an equal opportunity employer. Our organization believes we are stronger by embracing our diverse backgrounds and perspectives, promoting equity so all teammates can excel and grow in their careers, and fostering experiences to drive inclusion in our workplace and game. Golf is a game for everyone, and you are always welcome.

jobs.description: Employer: Packaging Corporation of America Expires: 10/18/2026 As a Fortune 500 company, Packaging Corporation of America (PCA) is an ideas and solutions company. Our corrugated packaging business seeks to be the leader in helping our customers — large and small — package, transport and display products of all kinds. Our white paper business delivers Paper With Purpose by providing the highest level of customer service and operational excellence. jobs.description: Employer: ArchKey Solutions Expires: 10/18/2026 Construction Management Intern - Regional About ArchKeyArchKey is one of the nation’s largest privately held specialty trade installation and integrated facility service companies. We design, build, and maintain electrical technologies and specialty systems that power the places where people live, work, and connect.We’re the POWER behind making the improbable possible, electrifying the nation, energizing the future, and bringing communities to life. Our work shapes what’s next, and our people are at the heart of it. At ArchKey, you’ll have the opportunity to learn, grow, and build a career with a team helping power the future.About the PositionOur summer internship program provides hands-on exposure to the electrical construction industry while preparing you for your career after graduation. Working closely with a project manager, you’ll gain experience across project coordination, safety, estimating, scheduling, customer communication, and financial performance. This opportunity is designed for students who are excited to build a career in electrical construction.Regional OpportunityThis position is based within one of ArchKey’s regional markets (New Castle, PA, Clinton, MD, Minneapolis, MN, Fargo, ND, San Jose, CA, Fenton, MO) and supports projects in the surrounding area. Your internship assignment will be connected to a regional office and may include work across multiple active projects, depending on business needs.ArchKey has regional offices and project locations throughout the United States. Visit ArchKey.com to explore our locations and learn more about opportunities in your area. Specific office, project, and assignment details will be shared during the interview process.Day in the LifeAs an intern, you’ll support the project team and gain exposure to the day-to-day work involved in delivering a successful electrical construction project. You may:Support project planning, scheduling, documentation, and coordination.Assist with estimating, bid proposals, purchasing, payments, and change orders.Work with project managers, superintendents, foremen, subcontractors, general contractors, and customers.Gain hands-on exposure to project safety practices and OSHA requirements.Help monitor project progress, budget, quality, and schedule.Assist with engineering and other project-related activities as needed.Minimum QualificationsCurrently enrolled in a degree program in Engineering, Construction Management, Project Management, Business, or a related field.Strong interest in pursuing a career in the electrical construction industry.Strong written and verbal communication skills.Ability to work collaboratively and build effective relationships.Strong attention to detail and commitment to quality.Prior construction experience is a plus.Experience with Bluebeam Revu, Accubid, or other construction technology is a plus.Ability to successfully complete a background check and drug screen.Benefits At ArchKey Solutions, our benefits package includes competitive health insurance options (medical, dental, and vision), a robust 401(k) retirement savings plan with employer match, paid time off and holidays, and access to wellness programs. Additionally, we offer professional development opportunities, tuition reimbursement, and employee assistance programs to support your growth and well-being. We ensure that our benefits are designed to promote the health, security, and work-life balance of our employees. Additional information is available at Archkey.com. Legal & Fraud Disclaimer All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or status as a protected veteran. We are an Affirmative Action, Equal Opportunity Employer.Beware of fraudulent job postings. ArchKey Solutions only communicates through official channels. All official communication will come from an @archkey.com email address and we will never ask for financial information, payments, or personal details outside of the standard hiring process. To confirm the legitimacy of a job, visit our careers page or reach out to a member of our Talent Acquisition team.

jobs.description: Employer: TADA Mobility (USA) LLC Expires: 10/19/2026 About ThrooTADA Mobility (USA), operating in New York City as Throo, is a Singapore-based ride-hailing platform that has disrupted the Southeast Asian market since its launch in 2018. Unlike traditional giants like Uber or Lyft, Throo operates on a zero-commission model. Instead of taking a large percentage of every fare (often 20% or more), Throo charges drivers a small, fixed platform fee. This ensures that drivers retain more of their hard-earned income and riders enjoy more competitive, transparent pricing.Powered by MVL’s blockchain, Throo creates a "fairness-first" ecosystem. By recording ride data securely and transparently, the platform incentivizes safe driving and high service quality through a token-based rewards system. Having already captured significant market share in Singapore, Cambodia, Vietnam, Thailand, and Hong Kong, Throo is now bringing its blockchain-backed, driver-centric model to the West, with New York City serving as the cornerstone of its North American expansion.About the RoleThroo is expanding, and we are looking for a Strategic Marketing Intern to join our foundational New York City Launch Team. NYC is the most competitive and regulated ride-hailing market globally. We need a high-velocity, intellectually curious individual to help build Throo’s brand from the ground up in New York City.You will work directly with the Launch Lead to create UGC content, design a localized messaging strategy, and execute the marketing playbook that will define Throo’s success in North America.Key Responsibilities1. NYC Market Entry & Messaging StrategyHyper-Local Messaging: Craft the "Why Throo" narrative specifically for the NYC market, differentiating us from incumbents (Uber/Lyft/Revel) for both driver-partners and riders.Segmented Campaigns: Develop bespoke messaging strategies for diverse NYC segments—from Manhattan commuters to outer-borough driver communities.GTM Execution: Support the end-to-end execution of the New York Go-To-Market (GTM) strategy across digital, OOH (Out-of-Home), and grassroots channels.Content Creation: Create User-Generated Content (UGC) or other marketing materials to onboard New Yorkers2. Stakeholder Mapping & AdvocacyInfluence Mapping: Identify and map key NYC power players, including TLC (Taxi & Limousine Commission) influencers, driver unions/guilds, and local community leaders.Partnership Scoping: Identify and vet local NYC brand partners (lifestyle, fintech, or events) for co-marketing opportunities that provide immediate "street cred" and user trust.Public Perception: Assist in managing PR efforts to position Throo as the "fairer" alternative in the NYC transport ecosystem.What You’ll NeedNYC DNA: Deep familiarity with the New York City landscape, culture, and transit habits.Creativity Mindset: Positive, experimental approach to content creationStrategic Rigor: Ability to map complex stakeholder ecosystems and translate "fairness" into a compelling, high-conversion marketing hook.Communication: "First-class" written and verbal skills; ability to hold your own in a room with senior leadership and external partners.Why This Role?Zero-to-One Experience: You aren't maintaining a brand; you are building one in the world's most famous city.High Visibility: As part of a lean launch team, your work on messaging and stakeholder mapping will be seen and used by Throo’s global leadership.Impact: Direct involvement in one of the most significant milestones in Throo’s company history.

jobs.feedName: Mike Curb College of Arts, Media, & Communication
jobs.title: Nonprofit Accelerator Internship at University Impact
jobs.description: Employer: University Impact Expires: 10/21/2026 Nonprofit Accelerator Internship – UI Charitable Outcomes Lab(Priority Applications Due 9.25.2026) BackgroundUI Charitable helps financial advisors and their clients give more impactfully. We work with ~1,300 families and ~400 financial advisors, and we manage $500+ million in charitable assets. More importantly, we have moved over $350 million out the door to nonprofits and impact investments working to improve the world's most pressing social and environmental issues. Why We Think This Work Matters NowTwo forces are about to reshape philanthropy. The AI boom is creating a new generation of wealth, and the founders and employees holding that ownership are deciding how to structure their giving. Most of them will want to move money out faster than the sector can absorb it. Over the same period, as much as $124 trillion will change hands through 2048, with an anticipated $18 trillion of it going to charity. We are building the infrastructure to turn that money into real improvements in people's lives. The Problem You Will Work on For This InternshipA lot of charitable dollars do not produce the lasting change donors expect. Plenty of funded organizations will never solve the problem they exist to solve, and money alone will not fix that. Most attempts to address this try to change donor behavior, including several of our own. So we are working on the organizations instead. What We Are BuildingEight years of building the infrastructure gives us a direct relationship with thousands of nonprofits our donors already fund. We want to help them become more effective. The closest analogy is a business accelerator for nonprofits, or a private equity operating team. We assess an organization across the core functions of a well-run business, run it through a cohort based program, and reassess later to see what moved. So far we have a literature review, a survey of 150 nonprofits, an analysis of our own data, and some first drafts of our curriculum and a way we will measure the success of the program. We will judge the program by whether those organizations actually improve, not by how many attend. The Eight Functions We want all organizations our donors give to, to have a sound understanding of their outcomes and impact. But in order to do that, you have to be running an effective/efficient organization. We are organizing the program around the functions that separate organizations that grow from organizations that stall. Each intern will own work across multiple of these functions.Fundraising and the growth engine. Treating donor development as a sales pipeline with stages, conversion rates, and follow-up. (Sales, Marketing, and Branding)AI adoption and operations. Where AI can take real work off a five-person staff. Marketing and branding. Making the case for support to people who have never heard of the organization.Board development and governance. What effective boards do, and how to get a board to do it.Program measurement and evaluation. Outputs, outcomes, and impact, and how small organizations can measure honestly without a research budget. (Public Health, Statistics, etc.)Finance, accounting, and internal controls. Who approves spending, who reconciles accounts, and what gets outsourced.Technology and data systems. CRM, donor records, and reporting that does not live in the executive director’s head.Talent and leadership capacity. Hiring, retention, and how a small team allocates the hours it has. Position OverviewWe are hiring two interns to help run a year-long pilot. You will work directly with Gary McHardy (a Rhodes Scholar based in South Africa) and Tanner Mills (Sr. Associate at UI Charitable). The team is small and the program is new, which means you will own real pieces of the work rather than support someone else’s. You will interview nonprofit CEOs, build the assessment instruments, write and deliver curriculum, and sit in on calls with the senior advisors guiding the program. Duties and Responsibilities:Design the curriculum. Build the workshop content, templates, and tools for your assigned functions, covering what the best organizations do and how a five-person staff can actually do it.Deliver it. Run webinars, cohort sessions, and office hours. You will be the one teaching, not just organizing.Drive results at the organizations. Work directly with participating nonprofits to implement what the curriculum covers. The goal is a CRM that exists, a pipeline that gets worked, a board that shows up.Interview nonprofit leaders. Run discovery calls, take structured notes, and turn what you hear into changes to the program.Analyze the data. Segment organizations by size, growth trend, and reported need using assessment results and public financials.Measure our own results and make adjustments. Track baseline and follow-up scores and report the delta honestly, including where we did not move the needle.The above list is not exhaustive; additional tasks will for sure be assigned as necessary. Required Skills/Abilities:Communication Skills: Strong written and verbal communication. You will be talking with nonprofit executives and delivering material they will read.Analytical Skills: Able to work with survey and financial data, draw conclusions, and present findings clearly and concisely.Project Management Skills: Able to handle several workstreams at once, prioritize, and hit deadlines without being chased.Comfort with Ambiguity: This program does not exist yet. You should be comfortable proposing an approach, testing it, and changing it when it fails.Team Coordination: Work very well with other people as a high output team. Deliver on what you’re responsible for AI Fluency: Regular use of AI tools for research, drafting, and analysis, with the judgment to check the output.Problem-Solving Skills: The ability to break a large, vague problem into pieces someone can actually work on.Humility and a Desire to Learn: A strong interest in understanding UI Charitable’s tools and programs and their role in achieving social impact.Integrity: Keep commitments, admit mistakes, maintain confidentiality where appropriate, and act in the organization’s best interests at all times. Education and Experience:Currently pursuing or recently completed a bachelor’s degree. Business, economics, statistics, public health, public policy, marketing, computer science and communications backgrounds all fit.Coursework, work experience, or genuine interest in at least one of the eight functions listed above. Tell us which one or two in your application.Proficiency with spreadsheets, survey tools, and standard office applications.Prior nonprofit experience is welcome but not required. Physical Requirements:Prolonged periods of sitting at a desk and working on a computer. The expectation is that candidates would be able to commit 20 hours per week, in person. How to ApplyEmail Tanner at tanner@uicharitable.org with your resume and a short note, under 250 words. Tell us which of the eight functions you would most want to own, why you want to work on this, and about anything you have produced, built, sold, raised, or automated. EQUAL EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITYUI Charitable offers fair and equal employment opportunity to all qualified job candidates regardless of age, race, religion, color, sex, marital status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, arrest record, conviction record, physical disability, developmental disability, national origin, membership in the National Guard, state defense force or any other reserve component of the military forces of the United States or Utah, genetic information, marital status, or any legally protected status.

jobs.title: MBA Marketing Intern at Graco Inc.
jobs.description: Employer: Graco Inc. Expires: 10/22/2026 The purpose of this position is to provide immersive, strategic-level experience within Graco’s Category Marketing team. At Graco, Category Marketing focuses on understanding and growing specific customer segments and industries (often referred to as market verticals), helping the business identify opportunities, understand customer needs, and shape strategies that drive growth. In this role, the intern will lead a defined strategic project for an assigned customer segment under the mentorship of the Director of Category Marketing. The intern will leverage market research, Voice of Customer (VOC) insights, competitive analysis, and go-to-market strategy to address a real business challenge. The experience culminates in the development and presentation of a strategic recommendation to Graco’s Executive Leadership Team. This internship is designed for MBA candidates seeking a long-term career in category marketing, product marketing, strategic marketing, or general management. Program Structure: This summer internship is centered on a high-value strategic project that addresses a real business opportunity or challenge within an assigned category and which has the potential to shape future growth initiatives. The project is supplemented by exposure to the broader category marketing function and close collaboration with cross-functional partners, including product management, channel marketing, corporate marketing, and sales. The internship culminates in a strategic recommendation presented to senior internship. What You Will Do at Graco Strategic Project Experience Lead a high-impact strategic project focused on a real business opportunity or challenge within an assigned customer segment or industry. Work closely with a Category Marketing leader to define the project scope, conduct analysis, and develop recommendations. Apply market research, customer insights, and business strategy concepts to address a meaningful business question. Develop and present a final recommendation to senior leaders at the conclusion of the internship. Market and Customer Insights Conduct market, customer, and competitive research to better understand industry trends and customer needs. Analyze Voice of Customer (VOC) feedback and other data sources to identify key insights and opportunities. Learn how customer and market insights are used to shape busness and marketing strategies. Cross-Functional Collaboration Collaborate with teams across product management, sales, channel marketing, and corporate marketing Gain exposure to how strategy is developed and translated into product launches, marketing campaigns, and commercial execution. Coordinate with internal subject matter experts to validate research findings and assumptions. Participate in team meetings, project reviews, and business discussions to better understand Graco's growth strategy. Professional Development Build skills in strategic thinking, business analysis, executive communication, and problem solving. Receive coaching and mentorship from experienced marketing leaders throughout the internship. Develop and deliver a professional executive-level presentation summarizing project findings and recommendations. Other duties and learning opportunities as assigned. What You Will Bring to Graco Currently pursuing an MBA, with an expected graduation date within 12–18 months of the internship Bachelor's degree in Marketing, Business Administration, or a related field Prior experience in marketing, business strategy, or vertical-specific market development (internship or professional) preferred Team collaborator with experience working in multi-functional or global team settings Strong analytical skills with the ability to interpret and synthesize VOC insights and market research into clear recommendations Excellent communication and presentation skills, including comfort presenting to senior leadership Ability to manage ambiguity and drive a project forward with limited day-to-day direction

jobs.title: Development Intern at Longroad Energy
jobs.description: Employer: Longroad Energy Expires: 10/23/2026 About Longroad EnergyFounded in 2016, Longroad Energy is a U.S.-based energy company focused on developing, owning and operating energy and digital infrastructure projects throughout North America. Longroad has developed or acquired 7.6 GW of renewable energy projects and has raised $20.6 billion of equity, debt, and tax equity to support completion of its portfolio. Today, Longroad owns 5.8 GW of wind, solar, and storage projects and operates and manages a total of 7.4 GW on behalf of Longroad and third parties. Longroad is owned by the Infratil Limited, NZ Superannuation Fund, Longroad Energy Partners, LLC, and MEAG MUNICH ERGO Asset Management. In 2027, Longroad will offer paid internship positions that create challenging hands-on learning experiences for college juniors, entering their senior year in the Fall. Selected interns will participate in a 10–12-week summer program that includes onboarding, structured work experience, mentoring, and exposure both to department-specific and company-wide personnel and activities. Job PurposeThe Development Intern will support Longroad's Development team in advancing utility-scale solar, wind and energy storage projects throughout the development lifecycle. Working closely with Project Developers, GIS specialists, and other cross-functional teams, the intern will assist with project schedule management, milestone tracking, project reporting, consultant coordination, and development data management.This role is designed to provide hands-on experience in renewable energy project development while helping maintain the systems, documentation, and project controls necessary to support a growing portfolio of development projects. Responsibilities & Tasks: Support the maintenance and update of project schedules, milestone trackers, and development work plans across multiple projects.Track key permitting, land acquisition, interconnection, and development milestones and assist with reporting on project status.Prepare weekly and monthly development reports, project dashboards, and portfolio summaries.Coordinate with internal teams and external consultants to collect project updates and ensure project information is current and accurate.Maintain project records, data repositories, and development documentation in company systems.Assist with organizing and tracking mapping requests, project exhibits, and development-related spatial data.Help prepare materials and supporting documentation for permitting applications, stakeholder meetings, and internal project reviews.Track action items from project meetings and support follow-up coordination with project team members.Conduct research and compile information related to project development activities, permitting processes, and local requirements.Support continuous improvement of project management, reporting, and document control processes.Collaborate with cross-functional teams including Development, GIS, Engineering, Environmental, Real Estate, and Transmission groups to support project advancement. QualificationsUndergraduate student at a 4-year collegePreferred major of Environmental Studies, Engineering, Project Management, Business or Energy related majorGPA of 3.0 or higherInterest in Renewable Energy Industry CuriositySelf-starterStrong written and organizational skillsMicrosoft Excel proficiencyCover letter highly preferredCompensationThis role pays $25 hour. OtherApplicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States. The Company does not sponsor applicants for work visas. Benefits of Working at Longroad Energy We are dedicated to providing our employees with the support and resources they need to stay healthy, secure their future, and be successful in their careers. Benefits at Longroad include the opportunity for merit-based salary increases, incentive plan participation, eligibility for our 401 (k) plan and matching, and comprehensive medical, dental, vision, life, and disability insurance. Our robust time-off policy includes accrual of 18 vacation days in your first year, paid holidays, and paid volunteer time. We offer paid parental leave to help support employees as they transition into parenthood. Learn more about our employee benefits. Diversity, Equity & Inclusion Diversity, equity, and inclusion matter - at Longroad, in our industry, in our communities, and in society at large. We embrace our responsibility to build and promote a diverse, equitable, and inclusive working experience and drive change where we live and operate. We work to actively promote and celebrate diversity, equity, and inclusion. We foster a supportive space that empowers everyone at Longroad to learn about, discuss and ask questions related to embracing and honoring identity. We collaborate with our community, colleagues, and industry in the ongoing pursuit of evolving and growing an inclusive and diverse environment. Learn more about our DEI commitment. Longroad Energy Values At Longroad, we SHINE. We aim to be the most trusted renewable energy company on the long road to a green future. We are an experienced team of problem solvers and promise-keepers who develop sustainable solutions that meet today’s challenges and make a lasting impact on people and our planet. Learn more about our SHINE values. Longroad Energy is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer (“EOE”). Qualified applicants are considered for employment without regard to age, race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, veteran status, citizenship, or any other legally protected status. Longroad Energy prohibits discrimination against individuals with disabilities and will reasonably accommodate applicants with a disability, upon request, and will also ensure reasonable accommodations are made for disabled employees. Longroad Energy is firmly committed to ensuring equal employment opportunities in all employment practices and personnel actions, including advertising, recruitment, testing, screening, hiring, selection for training, upgrading, transfer, demotion, layoff, discipline, termination, rates of pay, and other forms of compensation.Notice of AI Use in Job Application ReviewAs part of our commitment in creating a fair, efficient, and consistent hiring process we may use artificial intelligence (AI) to help our recruiting teams organize, summarize, and analyze information provided by candidates, including resumes, application responses, and other materials submitted during the application process.AI may be used to identify patterns, highlight relevant skills, and experience, and assist in comparing a candidate’s qualifications with the requirement of a specific role.
